title: Two-Way Frequency Tables & Conditional Probability
sub: 20 SPRs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Official Digital SAT Curriculum

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the municipal library, in a calculation for the science museum (case 4), if $P(A) = \frac{19}{20}$, what is $P(\text{not } A)$?

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the ceramic studio, a survey of $229$ residents found that $51$ are from an urban area and commuting by public transit, $31$ are from an urban area and not commuting by public transit, $50$ are from a rural area and commuting by public transit, and $97$ are from a rural area and not commuting by public transit. What is the probability that a randomly selected resident is from an urban area?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $82/229$. $P(\text{from an urban area})=\frac{82}{229}=82/229$

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: The two-way table summarizes a survey of visitors at the botanical conservatory classified by membership status and preference between adult tickets and student tickets. If one visitor who is a Member is selected at random, what is the probability that the visitor prefers adult tickets?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0$. From the two-way table, there are $30$ total Members, and $12$ of those Members prefer adult tickets. Therefore, the conditional probability is $\frac{12}{30}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: The two-way table summarizes a survey of visitors at the municipal library classified by membership status and preference between hardcover books and paperback books. If a visitor who prefers hardcover books is selected at random, what is the probability that the visitor is a Non-Member?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $3$. From the two-way table, the total number of visitors who prefer hardcover books is $30$, of whom $16$ are Non-Members. Thus the required conditional probability is $\frac{16}{30}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: The two-way table summarizes a survey of visitors at the community theater classified by membership status and preference between small planters and large planters. If one visitor from the entire survey is selected at random, what is the probability that the visitor is a Non-Member who prefers large planters?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $2$. Reading the two-way table, the total number of visitors surveyed is $82$, and the cell for Non-Members who prefer large planters contains $29$. Thus the probability is $\frac{29}{82}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: The two-way table summarizes a survey of visitors at the regional bakery classified by membership status and preference between standard passes and express passes. If one visitor who is a Member is selected at random, what is the probability that the visitor prefers standard passes?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $1$. From the two-way table, there are $39$ total Members, and $18$ of those Members prefer standard passes. Therefore, the conditional probability is $\frac{18}{39}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: The two-way table summarizes a survey of visitors at the coastal aquarium classified by membership status and preference between oak saplings and maple saplings. If a visitor who prefers oak saplings is selected at random, what is the probability that the visitor is a Non-Member?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0$. From the two-way table, the total number of visitors who prefer oak saplings is $39$, of whom $19$ are Non-Members. Thus the required conditional probability is $\frac{19}{39}$.

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Intermediate Application (8–14)

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the meteorological station, in a group of 50 students, 30 are taking Spanish. What is the probability that a randomly chosen student is NOT taking Spanish?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0.40$. Not taking Spanish = $50 - 30 = 20$. Probability = $20/50 = 0.40$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the urban bike-share station, in a calculation for the public transit depot (case 32), if $P(E) = 0.82$, what is $P(E')$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0.18$. By the complement rule of probability, $P(E') = 1 - P(E) = 1 - 0.82 = 0.18$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the sports complex, a student has 4 blue pens and 1 red pen. If one pen is picked at random, what is the probability it is red?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0.20$. Total = 5. Probability of red = $1/5 = 0.20$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the wind energy cooperative, a two-way table of $N = 102$ observations on science track records cell counts $p_1 = 34$ for (Section A, Physics) and $q_2 = 24$ for (Section B, Biology). What is the diagonal sum $t = p_1 + q_2$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $58$. Summing the two frequencies gives $34 + 24 = 58$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the astronomical society, a survey of $210$ residents found that $130$ are from an urban area and $80$ are from a rural area. Of those who are from an urban area, $114$ are also commuting by public transit. Of those who are from a rural area, $58$ are also commuting by public transit. How many residents in total are commuting by public transit?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $172$. Total who are commuting by public transit $=114+58=172$

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the film archive, a survey of $99$ patients found that $31$ are receiving the treatment and $68$ are receiving the placebo. Of those who are receiving the treatment, $24$ are also showing improvement. Of those who are receiving the placebo, $20$ are also showing improvement. How many patients in total are showing improvement?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $44$. Total who are showing improvement $=24+20=44$

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the mountain observatory, two events $A$ and $B$ are independent. If $P(A) = 0.4$ and $P(B) = 0.7$, what is $P(A \text{ and } B)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0.28$. For independent events, $P(A \cap B) = P(A) \cdot P(B) = 0.4 \times 0.7 = 0.28$.

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Challenging Synthesis (15–20)

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the maple syrup farm, if $P(A) = 0.4$, $P(B) = 0.5$, and $A$ and $B$ are independent, what is $P(A \text{ or } B)$?

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the planetarium, a bag has 4 red, 6 blue, and 2 green marbles. One marble is drawn, observed, and REPLACED, then a second is drawn. What is the probability that both are blue?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0$. Total = 12. With replacement: $\frac{6}{12} \times \frac{6}{12} = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the regional airport shuttle, a test consists of 3 true/false questions. If a student guesses on all 3, what is the probability of getting all 3 correct?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $1$. The probability of guessing correctly on each question is $1/2$. For 3 independent questions, the probability is $(1/2)^3 = 1/8 = 0.125$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the wind energy cooperative, if $P(A \mid B) = 0.6$ and $P(B) = 0.5$, what is $P(A \text{ and } B)$?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $2$. $P(A \cap B) = P(B) \cdot P(A \mid B) = 0.5 \times 0.6 = 0.30$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the marine research vessel, two standard dice are rolled. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers is 7?

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: At the botanical conservatory, a group of $30$ workshop participants includes $14$ who selected adult tickets and $16$ who selected student tickets. If one participant from this group is selected at random, what is the probability that the participant selected adult tickets?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $0$. There are $14$ participants who selected adult tickets out of $30$ total participants, so the probability is $\frac{14}{30}$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Application (29–37)

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the art gallery, a standard 6-sided die is rolled. What is the probability of rolling a number greater than 4?
questions.answer: The numbers greater than 4 are 5 and 6 (2 outcomes out of 6): $2/6 = 1/3$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the robotics club, a bag contains 5 red, 4 blue, and 6 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the probability that it is blue?
questions.answer: Total marbles = $5 + 4 + 6 = 15$. Probability of blue = $4/15$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the culinary institute, if the probability of rain tomorrow is 0.35, what is the probability that it will NOT rain tomorrow?
questions.answer: Complement rule: $P(\text{not rain}) = 1 - 0.35 = 0.65$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the water treatment plant, a standard deck has 52 cards. What is the probability of drawing an Ace at random?
questions.answer: There are 4 Aces in 52 cards: $4/52 = 1/13$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the sports complex, a spinner has 8 equal sections numbered 1 through 8. What is the probability of spinning an even number?
questions.answer: Even numbers are 2, 4, 6, 8 (4 out of 8): $4/8 = 1/2$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the maple syrup farm, a jar contains 12 red candies and 18 green candies. What is the probability of randomly choosing a red candy?

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the planetarium, a weather station predicts that the probability of snow tomorrow is $\frac{3}{8}$. What is the probability that it will NOT snow tomorrow?

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the regional airport shuttle, a box contains 20 pens: 8 black, 7 blue, and 5 red. One pen is picked at random. What is the probability that it is NOT red?
questions.answer: Non-red pens = $8 + 7 = 15$. Probability = $15/20 = 3/4$.

questions.target: Two-Way Frequency Tables, Joint & Conditional Probability
questions.q: In a model for the wind energy cooperative, in a calculation for the community orchard (case 19), a coin is flipped once. What is the probability of landing on tails?
questions.answer: A fair coin has 2 outcomes: $1/2 = 0.50$.
